answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to earn a slow, public work history before its votes count, with peers checking that history like a prism splitting one beam into many verifiable rays: a single operator spinning up a thousand clones would leave no real trail of completed tasks. Reputation then becomes an oasis that only genuine, sustained work can reach, and a sonnet of small verified deeds — not a flood of fresh identities — is what earns trust, so cheap copies starve while real contributors thrive.
